title: Recognizing the unit impulse definition
description: read δ(t) as an impulse at t=0 that is zero elsewhere and has total integral 1.

title: Interpreting impulse area instead of amplitude
description: interpret the impulse arrow as zero width, infinite height, and unit area rather than a finite amplitude.

title: Comparing continuous-time and discrete-time impulses
description: compare δ(t) with δ[n] and identify why the continuous-time impulse is not a value of 1 at zero.

title: Reading rectangular pulse parameters
description: identify the width ε and height 1/ε of the rectangular pulse δ_ε(t).

title: Verifying unit area of the pulse approximation
description: compute the area of δ_ε(t) as ε·(1/ε)=1.

title: Connecting pulse limits to the impulse
description: interpret ε→0 as width vanishing, height growing without bound, and area staying 1.

title: Interpreting the impulse as a generalized function
description: view δ(t) through its effect in integrals instead of ordinary pointwise values.

title: Reading scaled impulse weight
description: identify k as the total area and weight of kδ(t).

title: Applying impulse multiplication at zero
description: simplify f(t)δ(t) to f(0)δ(t) when the function is continuous at zero.

title: Reading shifted impulse location
description: locate δ(t-T) at t=T and keep its total area equal to 1.

title: Applying shifted impulse multiplication
description: simplify f(t)δ(t-T) to f(T)δ(t-T) when the function is continuous at T.

title: Using impulses to extract values
description: use ∫_{-∞}^{∞} f(t)δ(t-T)dt to obtain a signal value at a chosen time.

title: Recognizing the unit step function
description: determine whether u(t) equals 0 or 1 from its piecewise definition.

title: Connecting impulse integration to the unit step
description: rewrite ∫_{-∞}^{t}δ(τ)dτ as the unit step u(t).

title: Differentiating the unit step into the impulse
description: identify du(t)/dt as the impulse δ(t).
